simple.meaning: מֶרְכָּב (merkâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “a chariot ; also a seat (in a vehicle).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מֶרְכָּב (H4817) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 15:9, with occurrences in Leviticus, 1 Kings, Song of Solomon.

simple.summary: מֶרְכָּב (merkâb) / H4817 is traced through Leviticus 15:9, 1 Kings 5:6, Song of Songs 3:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a chariot ; also a seat (in a vehicle)
definitions.full: H4817. merkab מֶרְכָּב noun masculine Lev 15:9 chariot, riding-seat (properly riding-place ); — 1 chariot ( = following), suffix לְמֶרְכָּבוֺ סוּסִים 1Kin 5:6 . 2 absolute ׳מ , probably saddle Lev 15:9 (P). 3 מֶרְכָּבוֺ seat of litter Song 3:10 .

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘Whatever saddle he who has the discharge rides on shall be unclean.

Now therefore command that cedar trees be cut for me out of Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants; and I will give you wages for your servants according to all that you say. For you know that there is nobody among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”
